answer: A sybil farmer's profit is multiplication: one cheap script becomes a hundred identities, each claiming full rewards. So cap the pie, not the identities. Fix each epoch's standing budget as a constant — an ivory tower with one beacon — and split it among all claimants. A farmer fielding a hundred puppets divides its own slice a hundred ways, gaining nothing over one honest identity. Make admission a haven with a narrow door: a fixed number of new identities mature per epoch, so puppets queue for a scarce slot no operator can mint. Multiplication dies for lack of anything to multiply into.
